title: Nvidia Blackwell Tech Used at China Site Tied to Alice Huang
summary: A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker.

title: OpenAI Says Apple Pressured Suppliers to Shun Its Devices
summary: The trade-secrets fight between OpenAI and Apple Inc. is widening, with the artificial intelligence company accusing the iPhone maker of undermining its supplier relationships and using unfair employment agreements to prevent talent from jumping ship.

title: Verizon in Talks to Buy Fidium in $6 Billion Deal, FT Says
summary: Verizon Communications Inc. is in talks to buy the broadband operator Fidium in a $6 billion deal, the Financial Times reported, a move that would expand its network and allow the mobile giant to target more internet service subscribers across the US.

title: GTA VI’s Success Makes the Case for Human-Made Games
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI arrived after 13 years in development and it was made without using any generative AI according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick. It smashed all kinds of records. Gordon Bellamy, Director of Ethics at the USC School of Cinematic Arts, discusses what Rockstar’s blockbuster says about the value of human-made content in the AI era, why its extraordinary launch could reshape holiday spending across the gaming industry, and what smaller studios can learn from GTA VI’s success. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Poland Signs $300 Million Palantir Deal to Use AI in Defense
summary: Poland will use artificial intelligence-based software from Palantir Technologies Inc. to analyze battlefield data, bucking a push by some European allies to reduce their reliance on US technology for critical defense capabilities.

title: How AI Is Changing Black Friday
summary: Matt Shay, president and CEO of the National Retail Federation, says this may mark a step change in how consumers interact with retailers, as AI begins changing how shoppers shop on Black Friday. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: UK Pension Agency Takes Systems Offline After Cyber Incident
summary: The UK government’s Department for Work and Pensions took systems offline on Friday as a precautionary measure after officials detected a cyber incident.

title: Nvidia Blackwell Chips Turn Up at China Site Tied to Alice Huang
summary:
A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker. 
The gear installed at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia’s most powerful products, according to a serial number specified in documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November. Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral to obtain a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to filings from the lender that were reviewed by Bloomberg News.
Bloomberg's Tom Keene and Paul Sweeney get details from Olivia Levieux, Markets Strategist with Bloomberg News (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Black Friday Shoppers Turn to AI Bots to Find Deals
summary: AI-assisted traffic to US retail sites this holiday season will more than double last year’s, according to Adobe, demonstrating consumers are shifting from search engines to digital assistants. Bloomberg Intelligence's Abigail Gilmartin has the details. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Blackwell Chips Found at Alice Huang-Linked China Site
summary: A Bloomberg investigation found Chinese firms installed an Nvidia GB300 Blackwell rack at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, despite US restrictions on the hardware.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: SAP Struggles With Turnover in the Executive Team
summary: The software company is trying to fill big gaps in its executive team

title: Hackers Breached US Air Force’s Cloud Platform, Reuters Says
summary: Hackers breached the US Air Force’s flagship cloud infrastructure, called Cloud One, potentially putting large amounts of sensitive tactical and personnel data at risk, Reuters reported on Friday.

title: AI Data-Center Developer LIAN Picks London for $500 Million IPO
summary: LIAN Group, a developer of infrastructure for artificial intelligence and computing, has chosen London as the venue for a potential initial public offering next year, in what would be a boost to the city’s lackluster market for new listings.

title: Chip Stocks Look 'Very Attractive,' State Street Says
summary: Marija Veitmane of State Street says technology industry fundamentals have not weakened as much as the recent market selloff and outflows might suggest, and sees signs that sentiment is "normalizing." Speaking on Bloomberg Television, she says the pullback is an opportunity for bargain hunting, especially in semiconductors. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: SAP Weighs 10,000 Job Cuts as AI Reshapes Tech Industry
summary:
“The Pulse With Francine Lacqua” is all about conversations with high profile guests in the beating heart of global business, economics, finance and politics. Based in London, we go wherever the story is, bringing you exclusive interviews and market-moving scoops.

Today’s guests: Mohit Kumar, Jefferies Chief European Economist & Strategist; Ronald Lamola, South Africa Minister of International Relations & Cooperation; Alberto Nadal, Spanish People’s Party Deputy Economy Secretary; Carla Hobbs, European Council on Foreign Relations Madrid Office Head (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fed's Dec. Meeting May Mark Turning Point for Markets: Economist
summary: Mohit Kumar, chief European economist and strategist at Jefferies, discusses the outlook for the Federal Reserve's December policy meeting and its potential impact on markets. "My base case is that is the peak in hawkishness," Kumar tells Bloomberg Television. "That is, in my mind, the turning point for markets." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: SAP Weighs Cutting at Least 10,000 Roles in AI Restructure
summary: SAP SE is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions to transform its software business for the artificial intelligence era, according to people familiar with the matter, following reductions at Oracle Corp. and Microsoft Corp.

title: Nvidia, AI Fears Jolt Markets: Market Snapshot
summary: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, sending tech stocks soaring. But it wasn't enough to quell jitters in the artificial intelligence trade. Bloomberg's "The Opening Trade" spoke to global strategists and tech leaders about whether recent volatility signals a new era for AI investment. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stabilizing Forces Make Europe an AI-Storm Shelter: Taking Stock
summary: Europe’s appeal has far from dimmed for investors, with its stocks providing shelter from the wild swings driven by the artificial intelligence trade elsewhere.

title: Top Africa Fund Manager Buys Grit’s Embassy, Data-Center Assets
summary: Africa’s largest fund manager is buying Grit Real Estate Income Group Ltd.’s development unit, including its data-center and US embassy portfolio on the continent, with the property firm likely to delist from bourses in London and Mauritius.
